title: Americans need to get out of the house
gist: Yglesias argues that doomscrolling on X leaves people miserable while ordinary offline social activity (movie, kids' events, impromptu hangouts) brings real satisfaction; Americans should spend less time online and more in unplanned in-person life.

insights.claim: X's engineers are good at their mission of keeping users scrolling, which does not make users happier or help them achieve the goal they logged on for.
insights.speaker: Matthew Yglesias
insights.so_what: Engagement-maximizing platforms monetize attention at the user's wellbeing expense; regulatory and cultural backlash risk.

insights.claim: The author's feed on a weekend was dominated by French riot images, dunks on takes about them, and fights among people who agree Abdul El-Sayed beating Mike Rogers is preferable.
insights.speaker: Matthew Yglesias
insights.so_what: Illustrates how political-news cycles feed engagement loops.

insights.claim: Unplanned, imperfect in-person activities (a dumb movie with friends, a school debate tournament, impromptu adult-and-kids hangouts) produced more satisfaction than online time, and the author's point is that Americans should get out of the house.
insights.speaker: Matthew Yglesias
insights.so_what: Supports the 'anti-social century' narrative; in-person experience and community spending may be underappreciated.
